classification.difficultyReason: First interpret depreciation by $20,000 as a remaining value of $7,000, then form the reducing-balance equation and refine trial durations before rounding. Converting the stated loss into the formula's target adds a routine modelling decision.

content.prompt:
Leo has spent $\$27\,000$ on equipment to set up his painting business. The equipment depreciates at 18% p.a. Find how long it will take for the equipment to depreciate by a total of $\$20\,000$. Answer to the nearest year.
Hint: set up the compound depreciation equation and use trial and error to estimate n. Refine your trials around the target, then round the estimated time as requested.

answer.short: 7 years; the target salvage value is $\$7000$.
answer.worked:
A total depreciation of $\$20\,000$ leaves a salvage value of $\$7000$.
$$\begin{align*}S&=27\,000-20\,000\\S&=7000\\7000&=27\,000(0.82)^n\end{align*}$$
Using trial and improvement in the depreciation formula gives $n\approx6.80$. The time is **7 years**, to the nearest year.
